source.title: Sharp bounds for multiplicities of Bianchi modular forms
source.version: arXiv v2, 15 February 2024; publisher metadata checked for Annals 200(1). The full published PDF was not collated line by line with v2.
source.archiveStatus: The browser supplied the complete HTML text and accessible PDF passages. Downloading source bytes into scratch failed, including the dedicated download attempt. No original-PDF digest or local binary archive is claimed; this must be supplied at source intake.
readSections: Sections 1-7 in full via the v2 HTML text, including proofs and references
PDF text comparison and accessible page images; some diagram/page screenshot requests failed and no full visual collation is claimed
ST03 section 4 completion/flatness passages; AW13 sections 10-11.1 and 2.5; AW14 4.6/5.4 and their contexts
Marshall 2012 sections 2.1, 5.1-5.2; CE09 torsion/corank argument; FGT selected sections 1 and 4.17-4.20

summary: A section-complete draft inventory and routing proposal for Fu: integral central PBW bounds, analytic microlocalization and all-integral central injectivity, then rank-error and weight-aspect bounds via completed homology. Every missing item in this draft has one route. Retain checkpoint status until the primary-source archive/published-version comparison and the remaining scope/coverage checks in the handoff are completed. No mathematical formalization or proof-readiness is claimed.

conventions.local: Unless a statement explicitly varies this: p is odd; K/Q_p is finite with integers R; m>=1; G is the product of m first congruence subgroups of SL_2(Z_p); g_0=sl_2(R)^m; g=K tensor_R g_0; k in N^m; W_k is the external tensor product of Sym^{k_i}(K^2); D_k=product_i(k_i+1). A=K tensor_R R[[G]] has bounded-denominator coefficients. Completion of an enveloping algebra means completion of U(g_0) before p-inversion.
conventions.global: F has signature (r_1,r_2), d=[F:Q]=r_1+2r_2. A global weight kappa has r_1+r_2 even entries >=2. Delta(kappa)=product_real kappa_v times product_complex kappa_v^2. A real place gives local exponent kappa_v-2; a complex place gives two local exponents kappa_v/2-1 after choosing a completely split auxiliary p. Do not confuse d with the number of archimedean places.
conventions.status: library means exactly the stated narrow item is in a source file read at the baseline; planned means a named existing stage covers it, not that it is proved; missing means a source-qualified construction/proof is assigned below. Source proof issues never become assumptions that discharge downstream theorems.
conventions.sides: Modules are left modules unless explicitly right. Tensor products, annihilators, Ore fractions, dual actions and crossed products retain their handedness. M/Ann(W)M is an isotypic quotient, not an isotypic submodule.
conventions.genericity: The genericity and uniform-parameter arguments are used over Q_p with parameter locus Z_p^m. Finite K/Q_p is permitted for the explicitly stated coefficient-extension and affinoid-Verma comparisons. Do not infer the same compactness statement over an arbitrary non-locally-compact complete field.
conventions.dependencies: dependsOn records selected proof-critical item dependencies, not an exhaustive formal blueprint. Their directed graph is checked separately. A source-qualified theorem item is work to prove, not an assumed field that discharges its consumers.

items.name: The SL2 arithmetic quotient
items.statement: For a number field F and compact open K_f in SL_2(A_F,f), construct X=SL_2(F)\SL_2(A_F)/(K_f Z_infinity) and Y=X/K_infinity, retaining the real components and finite stabilizers. At neat level use the manifold model; changing level gives the actual finite covers.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1, definitions before Conjecture 1.1 and equation (2)

items.name: Algebraic local systems at cohomological weights
items.statement: With the global convention, attach Sym^{kappa_v-2} at each real place and Sym^{kappa_v/2-1} tensor its conjugate at each complex place; descend the tensor representation to a local system on Y. Specify its algebraic coefficient field and central parity before taking complex or p-adic realizations.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1, coefficient definition and equation (2)

items.name: Global weight-size function
items.statement: On the global even weights define Delta(kappa)=product_real kappa_v times product_complex kappa_v^2; the minimum in the weight-aspect bound ranges over the r_1+r_2 actual entries. On parallel weight Delta=kappa^d.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1, Delta and Theorem 1.2

items.name: Fu weight-aspect multiplicity bound
items.statement: If r_2>0 and K_f is fixed, there is C(F,K_f)>0 independent of every admissible global weight kappa such that dim_C S_kappa(K_f)<=C Delta(kappa)/min_v kappa_v. S denotes the cuspidal cohomological automorphic space, not all cohomology.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.2, equation (3); proof in section 7

items.name: One-degree saving at parallel weight
items.statement: Under the preceding non-totally-real and fixed-level hypotheses, dim_C S_(kappa,...,kappa)(K_f)=O_{F,K_f}(kappa^{d-1}) on even kappa>=2, with no epsilon loss.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.2, second assertion

items.name: Linear upper bound for Bianchi forms
items.statement: For imaginary quadratic F and any fixed compact open level, the cuspidal multiplicity at parallel cohomological weight is at most C(F,K_f) kappa. This is the proved specialization of the statement labeled Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction.
items.locator: Fu v2, Conjecture 1.1 and Corollary 1.3

items.name: Base-change linear lower bound at suitable levels
items.statement: For imaginary quadratic F and a congruence subgroup Gamma contained in SL_2(O_F), including sufficiently small such levels, the base-change cuspidal classes give dim H_cusp^1(Gamma,E_n)>=c_F,Gamma n for all sufficiently large n, where E_n=Sym^n tensor conjugate Sym^n. Use FGT Theorem 4.17 and the positive linear coefficient underlying Corollary 4.20 for the maximal level, then restriction and trace for a finite-index subgroup. Translate n=kappa/2-1 to the cuspidal-form convention. Keep this sufficient level class explicit rather than infer a lower bound at arbitrary adelic level.
items.locator: Fu v2, introduction before Theorem 1.2; FGT arXiv:0808.1204v1, Theorem 4.17 and Corollary 4.20, pp.25-27
items.note: FGT selected statement and proof passages and the page image of Corollary 4.20 were inspected. The full base-change proof, local type multiplicities and arbitrary adelic level comparison are prerequisite-paper work, not proofs claimed by this extraction.

items.name: Degree-one and degree-two Bianchi growth
items.statement: On the hyperbolic three-manifold at an admitted sufficiently small level, prove two-sided linear growth of the cuspidal/interior cohomology in degrees 1 and 2 with the specified coefficient system. Obtain the compact-support version only after proving the boundary comparison and its weight bound. The symbol asymp_{K_f} denotes upper and lower constant multiples, not convergence of a ratio to 1.
items.locator: Fu v2, Corollary 1.3 and equation (2)
items.note: Source issue S1: v2 uses H_c and calls it compactly supported while invoking a cuspidal Eichler-Shimura dimension identity. The support convention and boundary terms are explicitly audited rather than asserted away.

items.name: Integral and rational completed group algebras
items.statement: For compact profinite G form R[[G]]=lim_{a,U}(R/p^a)[G/U] and A=K tensor_R R[[G]], with convolution and continuous actions. A is the bounded-denominator rationalization, not the unrestricted inverse limit of K[G/U].
items.locator: Fu v2, sections 1 and 4, equations (4), (12)-(14)

items.name: Completed homology of the tame-level tower
items.statement: For a fixed tame level, form lim_s lim_{K_p subset G} H_j(Y(K_p K^p),Z/p^s), then tensor with K. Construct transition maps and the continuous completed-group-algebra action. Prove the allowed identification with the Z_p inverse-limit model rather than commuting limits with rationalization.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (4), section 7

items.name: External tensor products of symmetric powers
items.statement: For k in N^m construct W_k=external tensor product_i Sym^{k_i}(K^2) for the split product SL_2^m, together with the integral symmetric-power lattice and dimension D_k. Compare its group action with the differentiated sl_2^m action.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1 before Theorem 1.4; sections 3 and 6
items.note: Import field Lie-module theory from LieHighestWeight Layer 0. This integral algebraic-group/lattice construction precedes analytic distribution algebras; restrict its action to the compact group in the analytic successor.

items.name: Rank over the classical Ore division ring
items.statement: For a two-sided noetherian domain A, construct its classical Ore division ring Q(A) and define rank_A M=dim_{Q(A)}(Q(A) tensor_A M) for a finitely generated left A-module. State Ore localization and flatness hypotheses explicitly when using the same definition for another ring.
items.locator: Fu v2, Definition 2.1 and Theorem 1.4
items.note: Reuse Mathlib OreLocalization and its division-ring instance under OreSet, read at the pin. The noetherian-domain Ore theorem, localization exactness/rank comparison and this specialized rank API are not claimed to follow from the mere carrier.

items.name: Multiaffine polynomial bound
items.statement: A polynomial P in m variables is multiaffine if the exponent of every variable in every monomial is at most one. The growth theorems use a nonnegative-valued P on N^m of total degree <=m-1. This adjective does not mean a multiplicity-free representation.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1 immediately before Theorem 1.4

items.name: Algebraic coinvariants with a rank main term
items.statement: For a finitely generated Q_p[[G]]-module M of rank a, there is a multiaffine P_M of degree <=m-1 such that for every k in N^m, abs(dim H_0(G,M tensor W_k)-a D_k)<=P_M(k). The group action on the tensor product is diagonal.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.4, first inequality; section 6 proof

items.name: Uniform bound for all positive homological degrees
items.statement: For the same M there is one multiaffine P_M of degree <=m-1 such that dim H_i(G,M tensor W_k)<=P_M(k) for all k and all i>=1. Finite global dimension permits a common polynomial over the finitely many possibly nonzero degrees.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.4, second inequality; section 6 proof

items.name: Injectivity after every integral Casimir specialization
items.statement: For G=product of first congruence SL_2(Z_p) groups and lambda in Z_p^m, the microlocalization map Q_p[[G]] -> completed U(sl_2(Z_p)^m)[1/p]/(Delta_i-lambda_i) is injective. The assertion includes integral parameters that do not arise from a Q_p-valued torus character.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.5; compare Theorem 5.1 and Remark 5.8
items.note: Source issue S3: Theorem 5.1 proves an induced-character case. The all-integral extension is a separate item; coefficient-extension/affinoid-Verma inputs are recorded below, not a false identification of the two parameter sets.

items.name: Existing filtered-ring and filtered-module predicates
items.statement: Use Mathlib IsRingFiltration and IsModuleFiltration for increasing additive subgroups with multiplicative and scalar-action compatibility. Exhaustivity, separation and existence of a leading degree are separate hypotheses on these existing filtrations; this item does not claim new library theorems about them.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 2
items.note: Read Mathlib/RingTheory/FilteredAlgebra/Basic.lean at 082e2d3. These express the increasing filtration and compatible action. Separation, exhaustion and existence of a leading degree remain explicit hypotheses; no new carrier is proposed.

items.name: Associated graded and leading symbols
items.statement: Construct gr_F A=direct sum_s F_s A/F_{s-} A and the corresponding graded module. For a nonzero element of an exact filtration degree define its principal symbol. Identify products only with the degree/regular-symbol hypotheses that prevent leading-term cancellation.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 2
items.note: The real-indexed version uses an ordered subgroup of R, as in Fu; do not form a union of incomparable subgroups. Reuse the existing PBW graded object on its N-indexed specialization. The real-indexed quotient/module comparison remains additional work.

items.name: Strict multiplication by an element with regular leading symbol
items.statement: For an exhaustive separated filtration with exact degrees of nonzero elements, if the symbol of a is regular on the required side, then (Aa) intersection F_s A=(F_{s-deg(a)} A)a. Retain the right-sided variant separately by passing to the opposite ring.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 2.2 and its proof

items.name: Associated graded of a principal module quotient
items.statement: Under regular-symbol strictness, gr(A/Aa) is the quotient of gr A by the left ideal generated by the symbol of a. This is a graded module isomorphism; it is a ring quotient only when the ideal is two-sided.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 2.2

items.name: Completion of a saturated two-sided ideal
items.statement: For a noetherian ring A with central p and two-sided ideal I such that A/I is p-torsion-free, identify lim_a (I+(p^a))/(p^a) inside the p-adic completion with both completedA I and I completedA. Supply coefficient lifting and the Mittag-Leffler step.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 2.3, first assertion

items.name: Quotient and p-adic completion comparison
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the preceding ideal-completion statement, construct completedA/(completedA I) isomorphic to the p-adic completion of A/I, compatible with quotient maps and scalar inversion.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 2.3, second assertion

items.name: The existing PBW word filtration
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and an R-Lie algebra L, use the submodules of U_R(L) spanned by words of length <=n in the canonical Lie generators. The filtration is multiplicative and exhaustive; this item asserts neither ordered-monomial independence nor the full PBW theorem.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3, total-degree filtration used in Lemma 3.3

items.name: Field PBW and triangular decomposition
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field, the ordered products of a fixed ordered basis form the PBW basis, with the specified monomial formula; the associated graded is its symmetric algebra. Apply the split characteristic-zero triangular decomposition to sl_2^m.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3; section 5 Harish-Chandra and Verma arguments

items.name: Integral PBW for the split sl2 lattice
items.statement: Over R with 2 invertible, prove the ordered monomial basis of U(sl_2(R)^m), its tensor-factor decomposition and the multidegree filtration F_d with a_i+b_i+c_i<=d_i. The field PBW contract alone does not supply integral freeness.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 opening and proof of Lemma 3.3

items.name: The normalized sl2 Casimir operator
items.statement: On an R-Lie-module over a field K use ef+fe+(1/2)h^2 as the operator associated with an sl_2 triple. For characteristic different from two it commutes with the action of the generated sl_2 subalgebra. It is not a Lie-algebra element.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 Casimir normalization and Proposition 3.4

items.name: Casimir eigenvalue on a primitive vector
items.statement: For an sl_2 triple over a field where 2 is nonzero and a primitive vector of natural highest weight n, the normalized Casimir acts by n(n+2)/2.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3, lambda_i=k_i(k_i+2)/2

items.name: Central polynomial algebra generated by the Casimirs
items.statement: In U(sl_2(R)^m) with 2 invertible set Delta_i=(1/2)h_i^2-h_i+2e_i f_i. Prove centrality and algebraic independence, and identify the action of each element with the imported Casimir operator. The full characteristic-zero center/Harish-Chandra theory remains the existing highest-weight owner.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 opening; section 5 Casimir presentation

items.name: Integral and rational central reductions
items.statement: For lambda in R^m define U_lambda^0=U(g_0)/(Delta_i-lambda_i) and U_lambda=K tensor_R U_lambda^0. Construct the quotient maps and their coefficient-extension comparison; distinguish a two-sided central ideal from a one-sided cyclic quotient.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 definitions

items.name: Completed integral enveloping algebra and rationalization
items.statement: Construct Uhat^0=lim_a U(g_0)/p^a and Uhat=K tensor_R Uhat^0 with its Banach topology. Rationalizing precedes neither the p-adic inverse limit nor an unjustified tensor-limit interchange.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 definitions; section 4 equation (18)

items.name: Completed central reductions
items.statement: Define the central quotients of Uhat^0 and Uhat and construct their maps from U_lambda^0 and U_lambda. Prove agreement with completion of the integral central reduction using saturation, with the exact topology and scalar extension.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 definitions and Lemma 3.3

items.name: Genericity over the integral central-character locus
items.statement: An element delta of the completed enveloping algebra over Q_p is generic if its image is nonzero in every central reduction indexed by lambda in Z_p^m. Being nonzero or torsion-free over the unspecialized domain is not this condition.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 before Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 1.6

items.name: Uniform integral nonvanishing of a generic element
items.statement: For integral generic delta there exists N_delta>=1 such that its image in every integral central quotient is nonzero modulo p^{N_delta}. Prove the required semicontinuity on the compact set Z_p^m before taking a finite cover.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 3.1

items.name: PBW normal form after central reduction
items.statement: For lambda in R^m, the monomials product_i e_i^{a_i} f_i^{b_i} h_i^{c_i}, with c_i in {0,1}, form an R-basis of U_lambda^0. Prove reduction and independence with the integral central relations.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 3.3, basis assertion

items.name: Filtered ranks of the central quotients
items.statement: For d in N^m, the image of the multidegree PBW filtration in U_lambda^0 is finite free of rank product_i(d_i+1)^2, uniformly in lambda. Give the explicit monomial count, not only a rational dimension computation.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 3.3, filtered-dimension assertion

items.name: Quadratic-cone associated graded and domain property
items.statement: Identify the associated graded of the integral central reduction with the tensor product of the quadratic-cone quotients R[e_i,f_i,h_i]/((1/2)h_i^2+2e_i f_i). Prove the relevant noetherian domain assertions over R and over K, and over the residue field for p odd.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Lemma 3.3; reused in Theorem 5.7

items.name: Noetherianity and absence of zero divisors after completion
items.statement: For integral lambda and the stated complete discretely valued coefficient ring, prove Uhat_lambda is a two-sided noetherian domain by a separated complete filtration and its domain graded ring. Merely having a domain associated graded does not suffice without separation.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 3.3, completed assertion

items.name: Largest quotient of one algebraic isotypic type
items.statement: For a finitely generated left module M over a K-algebra whose image on a finite-dimensional W is End_K(W), define M_W=M/Ann(W)M. Prove its finite-dimensionality and universal property among quotients which are finite direct sums of W, with functoriality in M.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 and section 4 before Theorem 4.3

items.name: Dimension of an algebraic isotypic quotient
items.statement: When the acting quotient algebra is End_K(W), prove dim_K Hom(M,W)=dim_K(M_W)/dim_K(W), including finite-dimensionality under the hypotheses used for the cyclic quotients. Use the simple-algebra module equivalence rather than identifying M_W with Hom(M,W).
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3 before Proposition 3.4

items.name: The integral image in an algebraic representation
items.statement: For W_k^0=external tensor Sym^{k_i}(R^2), define E_k^0 as the image of U_lambda(k)^0 in End_R(W_k^0). Keep E_k^0 distinct from the full integral matrix algebra: they need not coincide.
items.locator: Fu v2, Proposition 3.4 and Remark 3.5

items.name: Bounded PBW degree generates the integral image
items.statement: For algebraic lambda_i=k_i(k_i+2)/2, the image of F_k U_lambda^0 in End_R(W_k^0) equals E_k^0. Prove the high-degree reduction on weight strings; the auxiliary scalar k_i(k_i+2)/4 in the calculation belongs to half the normalized Casimir.
items.locator: Fu v2, Proposition 3.4

items.name: The rational algebraic quotient is a full matrix algebra
items.statement: After tensoring the preceding integral image with K, the action induces F_k U_lambda(k) isomorphic to End_K(W_k) as vector spaces. The full acting algebra quotient by Ann(W_k) is End_K(W_k); the truncated filtration piece is not claimed to be a subalgebra.
items.locator: Fu v2, Proposition 3.4, rational assertion

items.name: Completion leaves the finite integral image unchanged
items.statement: The finite R-module E_k^0 is p-adically complete, so the completed central algebra has the same image. For every a>=1 identify F_k(U_lambda(k)^0/p^a) with E_k^0/p^a through the specified action map.
items.locator: Fu v2, Remark 3.5

items.name: Injectivity of a truncated generic multiplication map
items.statement: For integral generic delta choose a uniform nonzero reduction and its coordinatewise PBW degree alpha. If k_i>=alpha_i for every i, multiplication by delta maps F_{k-alpha}U_lambda(k) injectively into End_K(W_k). Prove this by integral reduction and the residue-domain calculation.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Theorem 3.2

items.name: Growth of a generic cyclic completed-enveloping quotient
items.statement: For generic delta in Uhat, there is a multiaffine P_delta of degree <=m-1 such that dim_K Hom_Uhat(Uhat/Uhat delta,W_k)<=P_delta(k) for every k in N^m. On k>=alpha first bound the numerator by product(k_i+1)^2-product(k_i-alpha_i+1)^2 and divide by D_k.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.6 = Theorem 3.2 and its proof

items.name: Uniform treatment of the low-coordinate strips
items.statement: For the cyclic module in Theorem 3.2, if k_i<alpha_i then its multiplicity is <=D_k<=alpha_i product_{j!=i}(k_j+1). Combine the finitely many such strip bounds with the large-coordinate estimate into one multiaffine polynomial of degree <=m-1. The union of these strips is generally infinite.
items.locator: Fu v2, end of proof of Theorem 3.2; explicit completion of its final estimate
items.note: Elementary deduction spelled out in this extraction; it must not be replaced by a finite-exception argument.

items.name: A nongeneric torsion quotient with full-order weight growth
items.statement: For m=2 the algebraic U(sl_2(K)^2)-module U/U(Delta_1-Delta_2) is torsion but has Hom multiplicity (k+1)^2 at equal weights (k,k), since both Casimirs act by the same scalar. Thus torsion alone cannot replace genericity in a degree-one bound. A completed analogue requires its own domain and quotient comparison.
items.locator: Fu v2, Remark 3.6

items.name: Ordered coordinates on an odd-prime uniform group
items.statement: For p odd and a uniform pro-p group G of dimension d, each ordered minimal generating set g_1,...,g_d gives a homeomorphism Z_p^d -> G by (x_i) -> product g_i^{x_i}. Prove G is a locally Q_p-analytic group and identify the power-subgroup coordinates.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 4 before equations (10)-(12); DDMS Theorems 4.30 and 8.18

items.name: The powerful Lie lattice of a uniform group
items.statement: On an odd-prime uniform G construct L_G using p-adic powers, the limit of p^{-n}-roots of x^{p^n}y^{p^n} for addition and the corresponding commutator limit for brackets. Prove L_G is finite free and [L_G,L_G] subset p L_G; form g_R=(1/p)L_G tensor R and g_K.
items.locator: Fu v2, equations (10)-(12) and following paragraph

items.name: Lazard Lie algebra of an open subgroup of SLn
items.statement: For a compact open uniform subgroup of SL_n(Q_p), differentiation identifies g_K with sl_n(K). At n=2 distinguish this rational identification from the integral equality established for the first congruence subgroup in Lemma 5.6.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 4.1; DDMS Chapter 9, Exercise 9

items.name: The standard p-valuation
items.statement: For p odd uniform G, put omega(1)=infinity and omega(g)=1+min_i v_p(x_i) in ordered coordinates. Prove the ultrametric, commutator and p-power axioms and that the p-power filtration agrees with this valuation.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (15) and preceding p-valuation axioms

items.name: Noncommutative ordered series for the Iwasawa algebra
items.statement: Writing b_i=g_i-1, each element of R[[G]] is a unique ordered sum sum_alpha c_alpha b^alpha with c_alpha in R. Its rationalization consists of series with uniformly bounded denominators. Construct the coefficient maps and convolution compatibility.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (13) and the following displayed identification

items.name: Locally analytic functions on compact analytic charts
items.statement: Form C^la(G,K) as the locally convex inductive limit of analytic functions on sufficiently small compact charts, with change-of-chart, translation and restriction maps. On uniform G compare this with analytic functions on the cosets of G^{p^n}.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 4 and section 5 before Proposition 5.5

items.name: The noncommutative distribution algebra
items.statement: Define D(G,K) as the strong continuous dual of C^la(G,K), with convolution from group multiplication. Prove the Dirac embedding, the differentiated U(g_K) action, their cross-relations and compatibility with the continuous-measure algebra K[[G]].
items.locator: Fu v2, section 4 and section 5 opening

items.name: Radius completions with weighted c0 coefficients
items.statement: For 1/p<=r<1 use norm_r(sum c_alpha b^alpha)=sup |c_alpha| r^{|alpha|}. The norm completion D_r has |c_alpha|r^{|alpha|}->0 as |alpha|->infinity. Distinguish it from the larger bounded-coefficient space D_<r; at all radii simultaneously the bounded and vanishing descriptions agree.
items.locator: Fu v2, equations (15)-(16); compare ST03 section 4, printed pp.18-19
items.note: Source issue S2: equation (16) omits the vanishing condition required by the preceding norm-completion definition.

items.name: Noetherian Banach steps and Frechet-Stein structure
items.statement: For uniform G and a cofinal sequence of radii in p^Q intersect [1/p,1), prove multiplicativity of the norms, noetherianity of D_r, absence of zero divisors, and flatness of transition maps. Prove D(G,K)=lim_r D_r and the Frechet-Stein property. Separate any assertion for arbitrary real radii from this rational-radius theorem.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 4.2; ST03 section 4, Theorems 4.9-4.10

items.name: Faithful flatness over rational Iwasawa algebras
items.statement: For compact locally Q_p-analytic G in the uniform setting and finite K/Q_p, the natural map K[[G]] -> D(G,K) is faithfully flat on the module sides used here.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (14); ST03 Theorem 4.11

items.name: The microlocal Ore set over an unramified coefficient DVR
items.statement: When p is a uniformizer of R and m=ker(R[[G]]->R/p), form S_0=union_{a>=0}(p^a+m^{a+1}) and prove it is an Ore set not containing zero. Construct the filtered localization and its completion. For ramified R obtain the needed algebra by coefficient base change, not by the same displayed S_0.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (17); AW13 sections 10.3-10.4
items.note: Source issue S4: if p is in m^2 then 0 belongs to p+m^2. Thus (17) with the maximal ideal is not an Ore set over every ramified R.

items.name: Lazard microlocalization is the completed enveloping algebra
items.statement: For the unramified coefficient setting of the preceding item, identify Q_gr(p)(R[[G]]) with the p-adic completion of U((1/p)R tensor L_G), compatibly with logarithms, exponentials and filtrations. After p-inversion obtain the flat map A -> Uhat; prove the finite coefficient-extension variant separately.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (18); AW13 Theorem 10.4

items.name: Microlocalization of a finitely generated module
items.statement: Define Mhat=Uhat tensor_A M and its natural map from M. Prove right exactness, and exactness from the specified flatness. Microlocalization need not preserve every module nontrivially; faithful flatness of A->D is a different assertion.
items.locator: Fu v2, paragraph after equation (18)

items.name: Extension of a finite-dimensional Lie representation
items.statement: For split semisimple g_K and finite-dimensional irreducible W with a finite g_R-stable R-lattice W_0, extend the U(g_R) action to its completion and pull it back to A. Prove irreducibility of this Lie A-module and identify its differentiated action.
items.locator: Fu v2, paragraphs following equation (18); AW13 section 11.1

items.name: Finite-dimensional semisimplicity in the semisimple-Lie setting
items.statement: Under the split semisimple Lie hypothesis introduced after (18), every finite-dimensional continuous A-module is semisimple. Prove the Lie-module and finite-image factors and their comparison. Do not extend this to an arbitrary uniform pro-p group with nonsemisimple Lie algebra.
items.locator: Fu v2, paragraph preceding Theorem 4.3; AW13 Theorem 11.1

items.name: Annihilators and the finite matrix-algebra quotient
items.statement: For the W of Theorem 4.3, compare its annihilators in U(g_K), Uhat and A. The first two quotients are End_K(W); the map from the A quotient is initially injective. Surjectivity on the A side follows from the finite-module microlocal comparison, not irreducibility alone over an arbitrary field.
items.locator: Fu v2, equations (19)-(20)

items.name: Recovery of finite-dimensional Lie modules after microlocalization
items.statement: For the finite-dimensional Lie module W above, every denominator of S_0 acts invertibly, and W -> Uhat tensor_A W is an isomorphism. Prove the corresponding assertion for finite sums and the compatibility of the annihilator ideal with scalar extension.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Theorem 4.3, equations (21)-(22); AW13 Proposition 11.1

items.name: Microlocalization preserves algebraic isotypic quotients
items.statement: For fg A-module M and the irreducible W with its stable lattice, the natural map M/Ann_A(W)M -> Mhat/Ann_Uhat(W)Mhat is an isomorphism. In particular A/Ann_A(W)=End_K(W). Prove naturality in M.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 4.3

items.name: Induced infinitesimal central character
items.statement: For a split reductive Lie algebra with chosen Borel and Cartan, use the Harish-Chandra projection with its fixed rho convention to send the differential of a torus character to a central character. Keep this induced-character condition distinct from an arbitrary integral Casimir eigenvalue.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 5 opening

items.name: Infinitesimal eigenspaces and central distribution quotients
items.statement: For a central character lambda, define C^la(G,K)[lambda] by simultaneous differential equations, and D(G,K)_lambda by the ideal generated by z-lambda(z). Prove the ideal is closed and the eigenspace closed in the indicated locally convex topologies before dualizing.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 5 before Theorem 5.2

items.name: Strong duality after infinitesimal specialization
items.statement: Under the compact analytic and Frechet-Stein hypotheses used in Theorem 5.2, identify D(G,K)_lambda with the strong dual of C^la(G,K)[lambda], using the strict closed-image duality theorem for the finitely generated central ideal.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 5.2, first assertion; ST duality cited in its proof

items.name: A locally analytic principal series
items.statement: For the compact split-group setting of section 5, a chosen Borel B=TN and locally analytic character chi:T->1+pZ_p, form functions f on G with f(gtn)=chi(t)f(g). Prove the differentiated center acts via the specified induced lambda, with the right-translation convention explicit.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Theorem 5.2

items.name: A nowhere-zero central eigenfunction
items.statement: Trivialize G->G/B by analytic sections on a finite clopen cover and use the character to construct f_0 in the locally analytic principal series which never vanishes. This is a locally analytic section argument, not a claim of one global analytic section of every flag variety.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Theorem 5.2

items.name: Density of an infinitesimal eigenspace in continuous functions
items.statement: For the induced central character, locally constant functions times f_0 remain in C^la(G,K)[lambda] and are dense in C(G,K) for the supremum norm. Deduce injectivity of A -> D(G,K)_lambda by continuous-measure duality.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 5.2, second assertion

items.name: The closure of the enveloping algebra at a radius
items.statement: For r_n=p^{-1/p^n}, n>=1, let U_r be the closure of U(g_K) in D_r(G,K), with its quotient U_r^lambda by the central ideal. Construct its normed ordered-logarithm basis and comparison maps as n varies.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 5 preceding Proposition 5.3

items.name: Finite crossed-product decomposition at a radius
items.statement: For r=r_n, show D_r is U_r*(G/G^{p^n}), and the central quotient is U_r^lambda*(G/G^{p^n}). Construct the action, cocycle and coset basis. The star is a crossed product, not a tensor product with a finite group algebra.
items.locator: Fu v2, Proposition 5.3 and proof

items.name: Logarithm and exponential estimates for radius steps
items.statement: For r=r_n, compute the norm of log(1+b_i) as p^{n-1}, use exp(p^n X_i) to place deep powers in U_r, and prove the finite topological PBW/coset decomposition. Every series is interpreted in its convergence domain.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, Proposition 5.3 proof, (27); Frommer theorem as cited there and in Kohlhaase 2007, proof of Corollary 1.4.1

items.name: Banach spaces analytic on deep cosets
items.statement: Define C^{n,an}(G,K) by analytic functions on cosets of G^{p^n}. Prove its Banach norm, compact inclusion into the next space, and C^la=colim_n C^{n,an}. Apply central differential equations in each space.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Proposition 5.5

items.name: A cofinal radius acts on each analytic Banach step
items.statement: Prove the deep translation estimate norm(g-1)<=1/p on a coset-analytic Banach step and extend the distribution action from the stated cofinal D_{r_{n+1}}. Evaluation at the identity gives the comparison with the strong dual, compatible with central quotients.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Proposition 5.5

items.name: Central specialization and the projective limit
items.statement: The natural map D(G,K)_lambda -> lim_n D_{r_n}(G,K)_lambda is an isomorphism in the section 5 setting. Prove this by the coset-analytic strong-dual comparison and cofinal radius maps; a tensor product does not commute with an inverse limit without this argument.
items.locator: Fu v2, Proposition 5.5

items.name: The integral sl2 lattice and the first congruence subgroup
items.statement: For p odd and G=ker(SL_2(Z_p)->SL_2(F_p)), prove that exp(ph), exp(pe), exp(pf) form ordered minimal generators and identify (1/p)L_G with sl_2(Z_p). Track the logarithmic normalization in every coefficient map; extend by products.
items.locator: Fu v2, Lemma 5.6

items.name: Domain property for central radius quotients
items.statement: For the product of first congruence SL_2 groups and integral Casimir parameters, establish that D_{r_n}^lambda is a noetherian domain. In the valuation proof set lambda_0=-p^2 lambda and choose 1/p<r_prime<=r_n with r_prime<p^{-1/2}; construct and prove separation of the quotient filtration before applying the graded quadratic-cone argument.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 5.7 and Remark 5.8
items.note: Source issue S5: the proof needs a separated quotient filtration for the weaker norm. Its separation/topological normal form is an explicit proof obligation, not a consequence of Lemma 2.2 alone.

items.name: Topological PBW normal form in a central radius quotient
items.statement: Identify elements of U_r^lambda uniquely with convergent sums of product e_i^{a_i} f_i^{b_i} h_i^{c_i}, c_i in {0,1}, under the exact logarithmic weights. Prove the coefficient-decay criterion, quotient separation and injectivity U_r^lambda -> Uhat_lambda for the indicated radii.
items.locator: Fu v2, last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 5.1
items.note: The paper leaves the normal form as an exercise; the quotient topology and injection must be proved together without using the desired injection to prove separation.

items.name: Grade does not change on restricting a finite crossed product
items.statement: For a finite crossed product B=A*H satisfying the noetherian hypotheses, compare the first nonzero Ext degree of a finitely generated B-module over A and B on matching left/right sides. Apply this to D_r^lambda over U_r^lambda; no commutative Krull-dimension formula is substituted.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Theorem 5.1; Ardakov-Brown 2007, Corollary 5.4

items.name: A nonzero multiple meets the enveloping closure
items.statement: For nonzero delta in the domain D_r^lambda, use positive grade of D_r^lambda/delta D_r^lambda and crossed-product grade invariance to find delta_prime with 0!=delta delta_prime in U_r^lambda. Retain the right ideal and multiplication order.
items.locator: Fu v2, proof of Theorem 5.1; AW13 Proposition 2.5

items.name: Injectivity for induced infinitesimal characters
items.statement: For the first-congruence SL_2 product and a central character induced by the analytic torus character as in section 5, prove A -> Uhat_lambda injective: first detect a nonzero element in a radius quotient, multiply it into U_r^lambda, and use the topological PBW comparison.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 5.1

items.name: A finite extension realizes integral Casimir parameters
items.statement: For lambda_i in Z_p and p odd, adjoining roots of a_i(a_i+2)/2=lambda_i produces a finite coefficient extension with integral a_i. This does not imply that every lambda_i is induced over Q_p: at p=3, lambda=1 would require (a+1)^2=3 in Q_3.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorems 1.5 and 5.1, Remark 5.8; explicit reconciliation for the AW14 route
items.note: Elementary root/integrality argument supplied by this extraction. It identifies a scalar-extension task, not a proof of analytic induction over Q_p.

items.name: Affinoid Verma module with an integral highest weight
items.statement: For a simply connected split semisimple integral group, odd very good p, deformation level n>=0, and an R-linear weight on p^n times its Cartan lattice, form the completed induced module from the chosen Borel. Specify the nilradical PBW coordinates and central character.
items.locator: Fu v2, paragraph after Theorem 1.5; AW14 sections 4.5-4.6 and 5.4

items.name: Central annihilator of an affinoid Verma module
items.statement: Under the preceding AW14 hypotheses, the annihilator in the affinoid enveloping algebra of the affinoid Verma module is the ideal generated by the kernel of its central character. For SL_2 products relate the character to a_i(a_i+2)/2.
items.locator: Fu v2, alternative source for Theorem 1.5; AW14 Theorem 4.6

items.name: Faithfulness of affinoid Verma modules over Iwasawa algebras
items.statement: Use AW14 Theorem 5.4: for its simply connected L-uniform group with p^n g=(1/p)R tensor L_G and n>=0, the affinoid Verma module of an R-linear highest weight is faithful over KG. At L=Q_p, n=0 and the first-congruence SL_2 product, verify the lattice equality by Lemma 5.6.
items.locator: Fu v2, alternative source for Theorem 1.5; AW14 Theorem 5.4 (including n=0)

items.name: Descent of central injectivity through finite coefficient extension
items.statement: For finite K/Q_p, prove faithful scalar extension for the bounded-denominator Iwasawa algebra, the completed integral enveloping algebra and its specified central quotient. Use integral roots, AW14 central annihilators and faithfulness to deduce injectivity over Q_p for every integral lambda, with the square of coefficient maps commutative.
items.locator: Fu v2, alternative proof indicated after Theorem 1.5; comparison obligations extracted from AW14 4.6/5.4
items.note: The deduction is the proposed all-integral route; scalar-extension compatibility is additional work, not a theorem already formalized here.

items.name: Irreducibility and self-duality at compact open subgroups
items.statement: For the split product SL_2 and W_k, prove absolute irreducibility and self-duality after restriction to any compact open subgroup used here, and agreement with its differentiated representation. Use Zariski density or the Lie-module comparison, not irreducibility for an arbitrary subgroup.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6 opening

items.name: Admissible Banach representations and finitely generated Iwasawa modules
items.statement: For compact p-adic analytic G and finite K/Q_p, use continuous duality between admissible unitary K-Banach representations and the corresponding finitely generated rational Iwasawa modules with their canonical topologies. Identify finite-dimensional continuous Hom and coinvariant duals on the correct sides.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6, citing Schneider-Teitelbaum 2002a

items.name: Algebraic matrix coefficients on the compact group
items.statement: Restrict K[SL_2]=K[x,y,z,w]/(xw-yz-1) to a compact open G and prove injectivity of restriction. Give left and right translation actions and the polynomial-degree filtration.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 6, unnumbered polynomial displays before (32)

items.name: Algebraic Peter-Weyl on a compact open SL2
items.statement: The degree-n associated graded of algebraic functions is W_n tensor W_n dual, of dimension (n+1)^2; obtain the bimodule direct-sum decomposition by complete reducibility. Extend by products and recover the maximal W_k quotient of A as End_K(W_k).
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 6, unnumbered algebraic-function decomposition before (32)

items.name: Hom multiplicity as dual coinvariant dimension
items.statement: For fg A-module M and finite-dimensional W_k, identify Hom_A(M,W_k) with the K-dual of H_0(G,M tensor W_k dual). Use self-duality only by its proved comparison. Establish finite-dimensionality and continuity of these maps.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6 before proof of Theorem 1.4

items.name: Weight growth for a cyclic torsion Iwasawa module
items.statement: For nonzero delta in Q_p[[G]], the cyclic left quotient A/A delta has Hom multiplicity into W_k bounded by a multiaffine polynomial of degree <=m-1. Its microlocal annihilator is generic by the all-integral central injectivity theorem.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6 proof of Theorem 1.4, torsion case

items.name: Finite cyclic filtration of a torsion module
items.statement: Over the noetherian Ore domain A, a fg torsion module has a finite filtration with cyclic torsion subquotients, each a quotient of A/A delta for a nonzero delta. Prove the handed annihilator convention and subadditivity of Hom dimension.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6 proof of Theorem 1.4

items.name: Multiaffine multiplicity bound for arbitrary torsion modules
items.statement: For any fg torsion Q_p[[G]]-module M, sum the cyclic subquotient bounds to obtain dim Hom_A(M,W_k)<=P_M(k), P_M multiaffine of degree <=m-1. The polynomial is independent of k.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6 proof of Theorem 1.4

items.name: Free approximation and a finite presentation
items.statement: For a fg module M of rank a over a two-sided noetherian Ore domain, choose an injection A^a -> M with torsion cokernel, and a finite presentation A^l -> M with fg kernel of rank l-a. Prove both assertions by localization and denominator clearing; a need not equal the number of generators.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 6, (33)-(34)

items.name: Homology of a free regular module with an algebraic twist
items.statement: For W finite-dimensional continuous and diagonal action, the continuous homology of A tensor_K W is W in degree zero and zero in positive degrees. Construct the untwisting comparison or the completed Shapiro argument.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 6 proof of Theorem 1.4

items.name: Dimension shifting with cancellation of the rank term
items.statement: For 0->N->A^l->M->0, the long exact homology sequence and regular-module acyclicity give H_i(G,M tensor W)=H_{i-1}(G,N tensor W) for i>=2. At i=1 combine the H_0 estimates for M,N and rank(N)=l-rank(M); the leading multiples of dim W cancel.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 6, (35)-(36)

items.name: Auslander regularity and finite global dimension
items.statement: For p odd and torsion-free uniform G, the integral and rational Iwasawa algebras in the source coefficient class are Auslander regular with finite global dimension. Use the grade and finite-resolution consequences; do not confuse canonical dimension with commutative Krull dimension.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1 before Theorem 1.4, citing Venjakob 2002
items.note: NE.0 names the Lazard/Venjakob homological programme but does not spell out this complete theorem. Route it as an explicit source addition to NE.0, rather than mark it already proved or create another Iwasawa carrier.

items.name: Canonical dimension zero gives finite vector-space dimension
items.statement: For a fg rational Iwasawa module in the compact analytic semisimple setting, canonical dimension zero implies finite K-dimension. In the finite-dimensional semisimple case only finitely many W_k occur, giving bounded degree-zero multiplicities.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 1 discussion after Theorem 1.4; AW13 Lemma 10.13

items.name: A completely split auxiliary prime and level refinement
items.statement: For fixed F,K_f choose an odd prime p completely split in F and outside the finite bad-level set. Shrink K_f to a neat level whose p-component is the product of the first congruence SL_2(Z_p) groups; construct the finite-cover pullback and characteristic-zero trace which return bounds to the original level.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 7 opening

items.name: Complex and p-adic local-system dimensions agree
items.statement: Construct the algebraic coefficient system over a number field large enough for the embeddings, then compare its finite cellular cochain complex after extension to C and Q_p (or the specified finite p-adic coefficient field). Flat scalar extension preserves dimensions. No continuous field isomorphism C=Q_p is assumed.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 7, (37); Marshall 2012 section 5.1

items.name: Finite generation and canonical topology of completed homology
items.statement: For the fixed tame-level arithmetic tower, completed integral homology is finitely generated over Z_p[[G]] and its inverse-limit topology is the canonical module topology. Pass to rational coefficients only after these identifications; the coefficient modules vary but this unweighted completed module does not.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, (4) and section 7 before (38); CC integrated decomposition, Theorem 1.1

items.name: Torsion when the real group has no discrete series
items.statement: For the semisimple arithmetic tower with r_2>0, prove the rational completed homology modules are torsion over Q_p[[G]]. Use Calegari-Emerton Theorem 3.4 and its proof via normalized cohomology growth and corank zero, plus the completed duality comparison. Do not assume vanishing of completed homology.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 7, citing CE09; CE09 Theorems 3.2-3.4; existing CC.5 decomposition

items.name: Finite-level homology from completed homology
items.statement: For the actual arithmetic tower and algebraic coefficient W_k, construct the convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence H_i(G,Htilde_j(K^p) tensor W_k) => H_{i+j}(Y(K_f),W_k), with finite cohomological bounds and the precise continuous-chain topology.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, (38); Marshall 2012 section 5.2, (34)

items.name: Dimension bound from the E2 page
items.statement: For a first-quadrant convergent spectral sequence with finite-dimensional terms on a fixed total degree and finite filtration of its abutment, bound the abutment dimension by the sum of E2 dimensions on that diagonal. Apply this without asserting degeneration.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 7, unnumbered inequality after (38)

items.name: Conversion of local multiaffine bounds to global weights
items.statement: Replace a real weight kappa by exponent kappa-2 and a complex weight by two exponents kappa/2-1. Then product_i(k_i+1)<=Delta(kappa), each k_i+1>=kappa_v/2, and a fixed multiaffine polynomial of degree <=d-1 is O(Delta(kappa)/min_v kappa_v). Prove all inequalities also when some kappa_v=2.
items.locator: Fu v2, Theorem 1.2 and final paragraph of section 7

items.name: Cuspidal, interior and compactly supported cohomology
items.statement: Construct the cuspidal cohomology subspace and its injection into ordinary cohomology, and the map from compactly supported cohomology to ordinary cohomology. For the indicated nontrivial cohomological coefficients prove the Eichler-Shimura dimension formula for the cuspidal/interior part. Handle the trivial coefficient system separately, and use a boundary long exact sequence rather than identifying the full compact-support group with its image.
items.locator: Fu v2, equation (2), Corollary 1.3; Marshall 2012 section 2, equation (4)
items.note: S1: Marshall defines H_c as a subspace of ordinary cohomology, not compact-support cohomology itself. The original Fu wording is preserved in sourceIssues.

items.name: Bounded boundary contribution for a fixed Bianchi quotient
items.statement: At a fixed neat Bianchi level the Borel-Serre boundary is a finite union of two-tori. For E_n=Sym^n tensor conjugate Sym^n, compute invariant vectors and the unipotent cochain complex at each cusp to bound every boundary cohomology dimension independently of n. Use the long exact sequence and Poincare-Lefschetz duality to compare the degree-one and degree-two compact-support, ordinary and cuspidal growth.
items.locator: Fu v2, Corollary 1.3 (missing support bridge); FGT section 1, equations (1.2)-(1.4); Marshall section 2
items.note: This is an additional explicit bridge required by the compact-support reading, not an identity quoted from Fu.

items.name: Existing Ore ring and module localization
items.statement: For a ring A and multiplicative submonoid S equipped with OreSet, use the existing ring A[S^-1], localized modules, numerator ring map and universalHom. For a nontrivial domain and S the nonzero elements, with OreSet proved, its localization is a division ring. This item supplies no theorem that an arbitrary multiplicative set is Ore.
items.locator: Fu v2, Definition 2.1 and section 4 equation (17)

items.name: Existing PBW associated graded and generator map
items.statement: For an R-Lie algebra over a commutative ring, use the PBW graded pieces, their direct sum and the degree-one generator map with its explicit quotient-class equation. This is not an assertion that the symmetric-algebra map is injective.
items.locator: Fu v2, section 3, associated-graded arguments

items.name: Upper rank estimate before higher homology
items.statement: From 0->A^a->M->T->0 with T torsion, right exactness of coinvariants gives dim H_0(M tensor W)<=a dim W+dim H_0(T tensor W). Apply the torsion estimate. No vanishing of H_1(T tensor W) and no injectivity on coinvariants is asserted.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 6, (33) and its following inequality

items.name: Lower rank estimate from a finite presentation
items.statement: From 0->N->A^l->M->0 and rank N=l-a, right exactness gives dim H_0(M tensor W)>=l dim W-dim H_0(N tensor W). Use the already established upper estimate for N to obtain the lower main term a dim W with subleading error.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, section 6, (34) and its following inequality

items.name: Central enveloping elements commute with distributions
items.statement: For the compact analytic subgroup of a connected split reductive group in Fu section 5, construct the enveloping-to-distribution map from differentiated translations and prove that the image of Z(g) is central in D(G,K), with continuous action and the compatible left/right dual conventions. This is stronger than centrality inside U(g) alone.
items.locator: Fu arXiv v2 HTML, (22)-(23) and paragraph after (23); Schneider-Teitelbaum 2002b, Proposition 3.7
items.note: The original ST02b proof still needs transcription; Fu reproduces the centrality claim. No proof is inferred merely from the enveloping inclusion.

prerequisites.citation: Ardakov-Wadsley, On irreducible representations of compact p-adic analytic groups (2013), especially sections 2.5, 10 and 11.1
prerequisites.why: Lazard microlocalization, the unramified coefficient hypotheses, finite-module recovery and canonical-dimension-zero input. Selected author-PDF passages inspected; the full proof tree is not an existing atlas blueprint.

prerequisites.citation: Ardakov-Wadsley, Verma modules for Iwasawa algebras are faithful (2014), Theorems 4.6 and 5.4
prerequisites.why: Alternative all-integral central injectivity route, including n=0, the integral highest weight and the faithful Iwasawa action. Selected statements and proof passages plus the n=0 page image inspected; finite scalar descent remains an explicit construction.

prerequisites.citation: Schneider-Teitelbaum, Algebras of p-adic distributions and admissible representations (2003), section 4
prerequisites.why: Noncommutative D_r, weighted-c0 completion, noetherianity, flat transitions and faithful flatness. Existing LA function spaces do not themselves contain these theorems. The radius-definition page image was inspected.

prerequisites.citation: Schneider-Teitelbaum, Banach space representations and Iwasawa theory (2002)
prerequisites.why: Admissible Banach-Iwasawa duality used in section 6. The primary arXiv record was inspected, not the full proof. Obtain the original theorem and topological coefficient hypotheses.

prerequisites.citation: Dixon-du Sautoy-Mann-Segal, Analytic pro-p groups, second edition (1999), Theorems 4.30 and 8.18; Chapter 9
prerequisites.why: Uniform-group coordinates, powerful Lie lattice and analytic comparison. Existing abstract profinite/pro-p foundations are imported; these analytic additions need the full primary source. Bibliography-only source selection here.

prerequisites.citation: Frommer, The locally analytic principal series of split reductive groups, Münster SFB-preprint 265 (2003)
prerequisites.why: The logarithmic norm/coset decomposition used by Fu Proposition 5.3, also cited through Kohlhaase Corollary 1.4.1. The original preprint was not acquired; its exact theorem locator is unresolved, not an independently verified Proposition 5.1.1.

prerequisites.citation: Ardakov-Brown, Primeness, semiprimeness and localisation in Iwasawa algebras, Trans. AMS 359 (2007), 1499–1515, Corollary 5.4
prerequisites.why: Grade invariance for the finite crossed product in section 5. Obtain the primary statement with its sidedness and noetherian hypotheses; Fu cites this result but the proof is not independently transcribed.

prerequisites.citation: Finis-Grunewald-Tirao, The cohomology of lattices in SL(2,C) (2010), Theorem 4.17 and Corollary 4.20
prerequisites.why: The Bianchi base-change lower bound and its level qualification are not consequences of the upper-bound theorem. Selected v1 passages and Corollary 4.20 page image inspected; the complete local-type/base-change proof and the published-version collation remain to acquire.

prerequisites.citation: Schneider-Teitelbaum, Locally analytic distributions and p-adic representation theory, with applications to GL2, JAMS 15 (2002), 443–468, Proposition 3.7
prerequisites.why: Central enveloping action in the distribution algebra. Primary record and Fu use inspected; original proof remains to be transcribed.

prerequisites.citation: Kohlhaase, Invariant distributions on p-adic analytic groups, Duke Math. J. 137 (2007), 19–62, especially Corollary 1.4.1
prerequisites.why: Fu uses its presentation of the Frommer norm/basis theorem. This is a bibliography link; obtain and pin the actual paper before claiming its complete proof has been checked.

prerequisites.citation: Venjakob, On the structure theory of the Iwasawa algebra of a p-adic Lie group, JEMS 4 (2002), 271–311
prerequisites.why: Auslander regularity and finite global dimension with the no-p-torsion hypothesis are needed in Fu Theorem 1.4 and assigned as a source addition to NE.0. The source record, not the whole proof, was inspected.

prerequisites.citation: McConnell-Robson, Noncommutative Noetherian Rings, revised edition, GSM 30 (2001)
prerequisites.why: Classical fraction-ring, flatness and crossed-product homological facts used by Fu. The generic Ore carrier exists, but its ring-specific hypotheses and theorems need primary proof references. This link records the cited edition only.

routes.title: Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas, Part II: integral and p-adic enveloping algebras
routes.brief: Build the integral and p-adically completed enveloping-algebra theory used by Fu, starting with finite free split sl_2 lattices at odd p and extending only in the stated Ardakov-Wadsley source generality. Import the field PBW, highest-weight, central-character and Casimir theory from LieHighestWeight (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight), including the existing Tau Ceti filtration and Casimir declarations; import Mathlib filtered-ring and Ore-localization carriers. Construct integral central reductions, their explicit PBW normal forms, saturated-ideal completion, image lattices in Sym^k, and the separated graded-domain arguments. Prove Fu Lemmas 2.2-2.3, 3.1-3.3 and Proposition 3.4 in declaration-sized parts. The growth endpoint is: a cyclic completed-enveloping module with a generic annihilator has Hom multiplicity in W_k bounded by a multiaffine polynomial of degree at most m-1, uniformly for k in N^m. Include the infinite low-coordinate strips, a nongeneric equal-Casimir counterexample, and the distinction between the integral image lattice and all integral matrices. Construct the affinoid Verma module and central-annihilator theorem in AW14 4.6 with its integral-weight, n>=0 and very-good-prime hypotheses. Distribution algebras and Iwasawa faithfulness belong to NoncommutativeAnalyticDistributions, not this algebraic core. Every definition gets a usable API and at least three tests; no extra characteristic-two theorem is inferred by notation.
routes.reason: The existing highest-weight roadmap owns the ordinary field theory, not these integral completions and uniform central-parameter bounds. This is a Part II, not a re-plan of the upstream roadmap.

routes.title: Locally analytic distributions, growth, and character spaces, Part II: noncommutative distributions and microlocalization
routes.brief: Extend LocallyAnalyticDistributions (LocallyAnalyticDistributions), importing its actual analytic Banach spaces, LF topology and strong duals. Import bounded measures and the completed group ring from p-adic measures, completed group algebras, and characteristic ideals (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0-L1), profinite foundations from ProfiniteProPGroups, and noetherian/grade inputs from NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0. Construct odd-prime uniform-group coordinates, Lazard Lie lattices, noncommutative convolution, weighted-c0 radius completions, Frechet-Stein and faithful-flatness theorems of Schneider-Teitelbaum. Construct the source-qualified Ore microlocalization and Lazard comparison with PadicEnvelopingAlgebras. Prove finite-dimensional/isotypic quotient recovery, the finite crossed-product radius description, central strong duality and cofinal-limit comparison, and the separated topological PBW theorem needed in Fu section 5. The endpoint is injectivity Q_p[[G]] -> Uhat_lambda for the product of m first-congruence SL_2(Z_p) groups and every lambda in Z_p^m. Keep the direct analytically induced-character proof and the all-integral AW14 Verma route distinct; the latter requires finite coefficient extension and faithful descent. Do not identify bounded coefficients with a norm completion, or use the unramified Ore set over a ramified DVR. Include Banach-Iwasawa duality and algebraic matrix-coefficient comparisons without duplicating field highest-weight theory. Require naturality, handedness, norm and quotient APIs and tests on the trivial representation, a ramified coefficient ring, and an integral parameter not induced over Q_p. This does not build Colmez or the geometric locally analytic-vectors theorem.
routes.reason: The existing locally analytic roadmap has function spaces and abelian transforms but no general noncommutative radius/crossed-product/microlocal theory. The same new foundation is reusable beyond Fu and must not be hidden in a Bianchi-only proof.

routes.title: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: weight-aspect multiplicity bounds
routes.brief: Build on Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces) and Completed cohomology, homology and arithmetic towers - Part II (CompletedCohomologyPartII). Import their actual quotients, algebraic local systems, finite chain models, completed homology, torsion theorem in the no-discrete-series case, and finite-level descent spectral sequence. Import NoncommutativeAnalyticDistributions and PadicEnvelopingAlgebras rather than reconstruct their rings. First prove Fu Theorem 1.4: for any finitely generated Q_p[[G]]-module M of rank a, G a product of m first-congruence SL_2 groups at odd p, the difference between dim H_0(G,M tensor W_k) and a product_i(k_i+1), and every positive-degree homology dimension, are bounded by one multiaffine polynomial of degree <=m-1, for all k in N^m. Split the upper and lower rank estimates before dimension shifting. Then for fixed level over a number field F with r_2>0 prove dim S_kappa <= C Delta(kappa)/min_v kappa_v, with even entries >=2, Delta=product_real kappa times product_complex kappa^2, and parallel bound O(kappa^([F:Q]-1)). Prove the Bianchi O(kappa) specialization; derive two-sided linear growth only with the FGT base-change lower-bound level hypotheses. Distinguish cuspidal, interior, ordinary and compact-support cohomology and prove the bounded-boundary bridge for the latter interpretation in degrees one and two. Include change of level, finite coefficient-field comparison, nontrivial versus trivial coefficients, and boundary normalization. No epsilon loss, leading constant, arbitrary-level lower bound or totally-real saving is asserted without a separate theorem.
routes.reason: Completed homology and the arithmetic quotients are already owned; the sharp weight-aspect estimates, rank-error calculus and their Bianchi application are genuinely new layers in this direction.

Attach Fu section 7 and its explicitly inspected Calegari-Emerton/Marshall inputs to the existing completed-homology contracts. The integrated CC decomposition already records the torsion theorem and spectral sequence. Its survey proof gaps do not justify a duplicate construction.

Make the finite-global-dimension/Auslander-regular theorem required by Fu an explicit source addition within the existing Lazard-Venjakob homological layer, retaining absence of p-torsion. The canonical Ore set of NE.1 is not the microlocal set or all-nonzero localization.

sourceIssues.locator: Fu v2 equation (2), paragraph after it and Corollary 1.3; Marshall 2012 section 2.1, equation (4)
sourceIssues.finding: Marshall defines H_c as cuspidal cohomology inside ordinary cohomology, whereas Fu describes it as compactly supported. Marshall also states the displayed dimension identity for nontrivial coefficient systems.
sourceIssues.resolution: Use the cuspidal injection for the upper bound. For the full compact-support interpretation retain an explicit boundary long-exact-sequence calculation and Poincare-Lefschetz comparison, treating the trivial coefficient separately. The two-sided Bianchi result uses the specified base-change lower-bound level class.

sourceIssues.locator: Fu v2 (16); Schneider-Teitelbaum 2003, section 4, pp.18-19 of arXiv copy
sourceIssues.finding: The norm-completion description of D_r needs weighted coefficients tending to zero. Equation (16) gives only a boundedness condition; Schneider-Teitelbaum distinguishes the larger bounded space D_<r.
sourceIssues.resolution: Keep D_r and D_<r separate. For example r=p^(-1/p) and coefficients c_(pj)=p^(-j) give a bounded weighted sequence of value 1 which does not tend to zero. At every radius simultaneously the two descriptions give the same Frechet space, but not at one fixed radius.

sourceIssues.locator: Fu v2 Theorems 1.5 and 5.1, Remark 5.8; AW14 Theorems 4.6 and 5.4
sourceIssues.finding: Integral Casimir parameters are not all induced by Q_p-valued torus characters. For p=3, lambda=1, a(a+2)/2=1 forces (a+1)^2=3, impossible in Q_3 by valuation parity.
sourceIssues.resolution: Preserve the direct induced-character proof separately. For the all-integral theorem adjoin the roots in a finite coefficient extension and use the affinoid-Verma annihilator and faithfulness theorems, with explicit faithful scalar-extension comparisons. AW14 allows n=0; this was checked on its page image.

sourceIssues.finding: With the maximal ideal and ramified coefficient DVR, the displayed union p^a+m^(a+1) may contain zero because p belongs to m^2. AW13 uses the unramified setting where p is a uniformizer.
sourceIssues.resolution: Prove the microlocal construction over Z_p or the admitted unramified coefficient ring, then prove the necessary finite coefficient-extension comparison. Do not reuse the displayed multiplicative set unchanged over every R.

sourceIssues.locator: Fu v2 Theorem 5.7 and last paragraph of Theorem 5.1 proof
sourceIssues.finding: The domain argument uses a weaker quotient filtration and the later proof leaves a topological PBW normal form to the reader. Quotient separation and coefficient decay are load-bearing, not automatic from an abstract graded-ring calculation.
sourceIssues.resolution: Construct the quotient topology, prove separatedness and the weighted normal form, then use the domain graded ring and the map into the completed central enveloping algebra. No certification of this proof interior is claimed here.

sourceIssues.finding: The printed minimum uses the field-degree index although the weight tuple has r_1+r_2 entries. The subscripted asymptotic symbol in the Bianchi corollary is used as a two-sided growth bound.
sourceIssues.resolution: Index the minimum by the actual places. State two positive constant multiples, not a ratio tending to one or a leading constant that the proof does not compute.
